topic.title: Test-Time Adaptation and Distribution-Shift Monitoring
topic.overview: Models deployed on changing data may need to adapt using unlabeled observations from their new environment. This topic studies sample reweighting, learned adaptation rules, continual adjustment, and monitoring of adaptation risks. The central tension is improving performance on current inputs without destabilizing previously useful behavior or reinforcing incorrect predictions.
topic.whyItMatters: Test-time information can reveal shifts that training data cannot anticipate, but adapting is itself a source of error. A useful system must recognize when adjustment is supported by evidence, account for heterogeneous users or domains, and measure performance over time rather than only on one static shifted dataset.
topic.evolution: A 2006 method corrects selection bias by matching feature distributions through weights. Adaptive risk minimization in 2021 trains models explicitly to adapt using unlabeled test examples. Later representatives benchmark temporal shifts and monitor risk; TiME in 2026 studies transport-based expert routing to balance adaptation and stability across changing language-model domains.
openQuestions: How can a model detect that test-time adaptation is making performance worse?
Which information should be retained when domains recur after long intervals?
